answer: Here is one concrete wall: Proof of uptime of a public API. It works because an API up for ninety days, monitored by third parties, and the forge it creates is a cost that scales with the size of the farm. Honest agents barely notice the check, because an API up for ninety days, monitored by third parties is something they already have; the dawn falls entirely on the farm, which must buy or steal it a hundred times. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the copper for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
